A file in a read-restricted field stays closed to readers of the record without access to the field
Field read rules the framework cannot enforce fail at boot
detail: An entity carried by a projection (`r.projection({ entity })`) accepted `access.read`, `writeOnly` and `access.read` on embedded sub-fields, but its queries are hand-written and the framework only strips fields of `r.entity` entities, so every reader of the row saw the field and the file guard released its files. Such a field now fails at boot (`projection/entity-field-read-rule`), on every entity a projection carries other than the `r.entity` of its own source (array source, a separate entity over an `r.entity` stream, a read model), also in `setupTestStack`. A separate entity that reuses the source entity's `fields` object under another name or table counts as separate. The entity-level `access.read` of a read model is unchanged. The cross-tenant file read asks only whether the declared query returns the record, so an entity with `crossTenantFileRead` and a file field (or embedded file sub-field) with an `access.read` rule fails at boot (`files/cross-tenant-read-restricted-file-field`); fields added by a registrar extension through `extendSchema` count, checked when the registry is built. `crossTenantFileRead` on a read-model entity, which the file routes already honour, is validated at boot with the same rules as on an entity (reason, registered query, no read-restricted file field); on a projection entity the file routes never look up (array source, or a source stream that an `r.entity` of the app registers) it fails at boot (`files/cross-tenant-read-unseen-projection-entity`) instead of being ignored. A field that a registrar extension adds through `extendSchema` with `access.read` or `writeOnly` now counts for the registry check too, so a query handler of that feature that is not bound to an entity must declare `resultEntity` or `unfilteredResult`, as for the entity's own fields.
migration: For `projection/entity-field-read-rule`, drop the field's `access.read` or `writeOnly` on the read-model entity and restrict the read model's query access instead, or keep the field on an `r.entity`. For `files/cross-tenant-read-restricted-file-field`, drop the file field's `access.read` or the entity's `crossTenantFileRead`. For `files/cross-tenant-read-unseen-projection-entity`, move `crossTenantFileRead` to the `r.entity` of the source stream. For the `resultEntity` error, add `resultEntity` (or `unfilteredResult` with a reason) to the query handler the error names.

title: Rebuild guards the single-table contract
detail: During a rebuild only the projection's own table points at the shadow schema; any other table an apply writes is the live table, so a multi-table apply corrupted live data during an online rebuild. Single-stream and multi-stream rebuilds now compare `pg_stat_xact_user_tables` before and after the replay and abort the rebuild transaction, naming the tables, if any table outside the rebuild schema was written.
migration: A projection or multi-stream projection whose apply writes a second table must split that write into its own projection or a side-effect consumer; until then its rebuild fails with the table name.

title: Event pruning removes whole streams only
detail: `pruneEvents` used to delete every event older than the cutoff, so a long-lived aggregate lost its old `.created` event while newer `.updated` events stayed. The next rebuild then dropped the row silently, because an update without a row is a no-op and the ghost-row guard only asks for any event. Now a stream (tenant, aggregate id) is pruned only when all of its events are older than the cutoff, and then completely. `batchSize` limits whole streams per call instead of single events, so a batch never cuts a stream; `deletedCount` still counts events and can exceed `batchSize`. Loops that stop when `deletedCount < batchSize` keep terminating.
migration: Retention jobs that relied on trimming old events from streams that are still active get fewer deletions; to shrink active streams, archive or snapshot them instead. Callers that compared `deletedCount` with an exact per-call event limit must treat `batchSize` as a stream limit.

detail: `r.job` with `trigger: { on: "<feature>:write:<handler>" }` received only the handler's input payload, so a follow-up job could not tell which row was created and had to sweep the tenant. When the handler returns a save or delete lifecycle result (every `r.crud` verb and executor write), the job now gets `ctx.triggerEvent = { id, aggregateId, headers }` of that event; `aggregateId` is the written row's id. Handlers that return plain data still run the job without `triggerEvent`. `JobTriggerEvent` gained the required field `aggregateId`, also on the job-trigger and catch-up consumer paths.
migration: Code that builds a `JobTriggerEvent` itself, for example a test calling `jobRunner.handleCatchUpEvent(...)`, adds `aggregateId` (the stored event's `aggregateId`). Jobs that swept the tenant because the id was missing can read `ctx.triggerEvent?.aggregateId` instead.

Lean update, delete and forget events and executor createMany/updateMany
detail: The `<entity>.updated` event now carries `previous` with the old values of exactly the keys in `changes` (owner-transition rekeys included) instead of the whole pre-update row. `<entity>.deleted` and `<entity>.forgotten` carry `previous` without personal, encrypted and sensitive fields, in plaintext and without a KMS call, so the erasure event no longer holds a copy of the erased values and a delete without a KMS no longer writes personal fields in plaintext to the log. A delete of a row whose subject key is already erased now succeeds without an erasure purpose; restoring that row stays refused. Restore still carries the whole row, and the update and delete WriteResults still return the whole row. The search index reads the live row on update, the access invalidation of `tenant-membership.updated` reads the user id from the changes or the membership row, and the derived webhook contract of `updated` no longer has `id` inside `previous`; the `deleted` webhook no longer passes tenant-key ciphertext of non-personal tenant-owned fields. `EventStoreExecutor` has `createMany` and `updateMany`: every row runs the checks of create and update, all events go into the log with one statement and one optimistic check per stream, and the batch commits or fails as a whole. Append and projection of a single create or update share one savepoint. `createAccessInvalidationEventConsumer` takes the registry as second argument. A forgotten file reference now lowers the tenant storage usage.
migration: Code that reads `payload.previous` of an `updated` event for a key the event did not change reads the projection row instead. Code that reads a personal, encrypted or sensitive field from `payload.previous` of a `deleted` or `forgotten` event reads it from the `created` and `updated` events or the projection row before the delete; events written before this release still carry the whole row. Webhook receivers of `<entity>.updated` take the id from the top level. Hand-built `EventStoreExecutor` objects add `createMany` and `updateMany`. A loop of `executor.create` or `executor.update` over many rows in one handler can switch to `createMany` or `updateMany`.

title: Named entity verbs, executor history and listAsOf
detail: An entity declares named update events in `verbs`, optionally with a transition (`{ archived: { transition: { field: "status", from: ["open"], to: "archived" } } }`). `executor.update(payload, user, db, { verb })` appends `<entity>.<verb>` with the `{ changes, previous }` payload of `updated`; a verb with a transition sets its field and fails with `invalid_transition` (422) when the current state is not in `from`. The implicit projection, rebuild, entity upcasters, job triggers, projection apply keys, derived webhook contracts and the audit filter treat a declared verb like `updated`. Boot rejects lifecycle names, names with dots, transitions on non-select fields, unknown options and pairs that `entity.transitions` does not allow. `EventStoreExecutor` has `history({ id })`, which returns the lifecycle and verb events of one entity as `{ version, at, by, verb, changes }`, upcast and decrypted, without fields the caller may not read, and `listAsOf({ asOf })`, which folds the entity's events up to an instant into rows and refuses entities with parentRef, readGate or a row read ownership.
migration: Hand-built `EventStoreExecutor` objects add `history` and `listAsOf`. A status change written as its own `r.defineEvent` plus an `extendEntityProjection` or `setFields` apply can become a verb in the entity's `verbs` and an `executor.update(..., { verb })`; the projection apply and the hand-written transition check go away. Code that reads `kumiko_events` to show an entity's changes or to fold it to a past instant switches to `executor.history` or `executor.listAsOf`.

title: Entity list queries read only the requested fields

detail: A domain event appended through `ctx.events.append`, `appendOne`, a job or a multi-stream apply on an entity row's stream (aggregate type equals the entity name) now sets the row's `version` to the event's version in the same transaction, and a rebuild of the entity's implicit projection restores it from the event log. List and detail return `row.version` and no longer run a correlated `MAX(version)` subquery against `kumiko_events` for every row. Writes keep reading the stream version for their optimistic lock. Events appended without the projection pipeline (event-store `append`, `appendEventInTenantDb` without `registry`) do not move the row version.
migration: Rows that received domain events before this release kept their old version; `runProdApp` and `runWorkerApp` now align them with their stream on every boot in the background (only the `read_*` rows change, the event log stays untouched), so no rebuild by hand is needed. It works in id batches of short transactions with a short lock_timeout; a table that hits the lock_timeout or fails is logged and finished on the next boot, and until then editing such a row can still fail with `version_conflict`. The same repair is exported as `alignLiveRowVersionsWithStreams(db, tableName, aggregateTypes, systemStream, { batchSize, signal })` from `@cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/db` for apps that boot without `runProdApp` or `runWorkerApp`. Append domain events on an entity row's stream with the entity name as aggregate type and through `ctx.events.append`, not through the event-store `append`.

title: changes.json keeps detail only on breaking entries
One KMS key lookup per subject when decrypting several PII fields
App connections carry their projection registry
detail: The prod boot, the worker boot and `setupTestStack` bind both database pools to the app registry with the new `bindAppProjectionRegistry(connection, registry)` from `@cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/db`. Every transaction, savepoint and reserved connection derived from them inherits it, so `createTenantDb({ db: tx, ... })` inside a multi-stream projection apply or a raw `transaction()` runs the custom projections of an executor write, as the dispatcher's own TenantDb already did. User-data delete and export hooks get a TenantDb with the registry, so `executor.forget(id, user, ctx.db)` in a forget hook also clears child projections for the `<entity>.forgotten` event. Binding a connection to a second, different registry throws. Connections that are never bound (CLI tools, a bare `createTestDb`) keep skipping custom projections.
migration: Remove manual `runProjectionsForEvent(...)` calls that follow an executor write (create, update, delete, forget) on a TenantDb built over an app connection, together with the `unsafeRaw()` grant and escape hatch they needed; the executor has already projected that event object, so the manual call is a no-op. Raw `append(...)` plus `runProjectionsForEvent` stays as it is.

title: ctx.db rows are typed from the entity table
detail: Without an explicit type argument, `ctx.db.selectMany(table)` and `ctx.db.fetchOne(table, where)` on a table from `buildEntityTable` or `createEntityExecutor` now return the table's column row (`EntityColumnRow<E>`): every field with its column type, money and locatedTimestamp as their column pair, personal values as stored. `createEntityExecutor` returns `table: EntityTable<E>` instead of the widened `EntityTable`. `EntityRow` and `EntityColumnRow` are exported from the db entry point. An explicit type argument, `options.fields` and tables without entity typing keep `Record<string, unknown>`.
migration: Code that read such rows as `Record<string, unknown>` can now fail to compile where it reads a key the table does not have or assigns the row to an incompatible type. Drop the casts and read the typed fields, or pass the row type explicitly.

title: ctx.db.unsafeRaw() stays in the caller's tenant
detail: A granted `ctx.db.unsafeRaw()` used to run in the system scope of row level security, so raw SQL with a forgotten tenant_id filter read and wrote rows of every tenant. It now runs in the scope of its TenantDb: the caller's tenant (plus system tenant rows on tables that allow reading them) in tenant mode, the system scope in system mode. The new `ctx.db.unsafeRawAllTenants()` returns the old all-tenants runner under the same `unsafeRaw` grant and audit. `ctx.systemDb.unsafeRaw(reason)` is unchanged. `ConnectionTenantDb` has both methods.
migration: Run kumiko-upgrade --apply; the unsafe-raw-all-tenants codemod renames every `.unsafeRaw()` call without arguments to `.unsafeRawAllTenants()`, which keeps today's behaviour. Hand-written TenantDb stubs it lists need an `unsafeRawAllTenants` member. Switch a call back to `unsafeRaw()` where its SQL only touches the caller's own tenant.

title: ctx.db.upsert counts atomically with increment
createTenantDb on the db subpath is tenant-only
detail: `createTenantDb` from `@cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/db` takes `{ db, tenantId, tracer?, meter?, signal?, mode?: "tenant" }` and always builds a tenant-mode handle. `mode: "system"`, `reason` and `grants` are no longer accepted there. The full function lives in `@cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/internal/row-level-security` for framework packages and in `@cosmicdrift/kumiko-testing/helpers` for tests, and the guard `internal-subpath-imports` keeps the helpers export out of production files. The public `createTenantDb` throws `AccessDeniedError` when its runner comes from `ctx.db.unsafeRaw()`, `ctx.db.unsafeRawAllTenants()` or `ctx.systemDb.unsafeRaw(reason)`, also for a transaction, savepoint or reserved connection opened on such a runner, and `scopeTenantDbToTenant` throws `AccessDeniedError` when it would move a tenant-mode handle to another tenant. Declared cross-tenant access stays on `r.systemScope()` with `ctx.systemDb.acknowledgeCrossTenant(reason)`, the escape hatch grant `crossTenantReads` with `ctx.crossTenantReads`, and `ctx.tenants.writeTarget(tenantId)`.
migration: Handlers, hooks and jobs that built `createTenantDb({ mode: "system", ... })` or `createTenantDb({ db: ctx.db.unsafeRaw(), tenantId })` for another tenant move to `r.systemScope()` with `ctx.systemDb.acknowledgeCrossTenant(reason)`, to `ctx.crossTenantReads` for reads, or to `ctx.tenants.writeTarget(tenantId)` for SystemAdmin writes into one tenant. Boot code, backfills and CLIs that hold a `DbConnection` call `createTenantDb({ db, tenantId })` once per target tenant. Tests that need `mode: "system"` or `grants` import `createTenantDb` from `@cosmicdrift/kumiko-testing/helpers`.

title: Every event append states its concurrency expectation
detail: ctx.events.append, unsafeAppend, tryAppend, emitEvent, the job ctx.events.append, the MSP appendEvent and unsafeAppendEvent and r.step.aggregate.appendEvent now require either expectedVersion or blindAppendReason (type AppendConcurrency from @cosmicdrift/kumiko-types/handlers). Before, the stream version was read at append time, so a handler that read state and then appended could silently stack on a decision another transaction had just committed. An append with neither field, a negative or non-integer expectedVersion, or a placeholder reason (todo, legacy, n/a, ...) throws internal_error. With expectedVersion a concurrent append fails with 409 version_conflict (tryAppend returns ok:false). unsafeAppend now only means an untyped payload; the typed path is emitEvent(ctx, eventDef, ...). The bundled workflow runner pins its resume claim, so a step can no longer be resumed twice when two dispatches race.
migration: At every append site pick one: (1) the handler reads state of the aggregate before appending: call const v = await ctx.events.streamVersion(aggregateId) as the first statement before that read (projection row, executor detail or ctx.events.load) and pass expectedVersion: v (v + 1 for a second append in the same handler), or append through a ctx.events.fetchForWriting handle; (2) the aggregate id was created in this handler: expectedVersion: 0; (3) the event is valid whatever was appended meanwhile: blindAppendReason with a concrete sentence. Clients treat 409 version_conflict like a stale form: reload and retry. Known sites: solon 35, publicstatus 6, kumiko-enterprise 2, money-horse 1.

title: Free query helpers are typed
detail: `TableLike` was `EntityTableMeta | any`, `AnyDb` was `DbRunner | unknown` and rows defaulted to `any`, so the type check was off for every free query call. `TableLike` is now `SchemaTable | EntityTableMeta`, `AnyDb` is `DbRunner | TenantDb`, and the default row is `Record<string, unknown>`. `selectMany` and `fetchOne` derive the row from a table built from an entity, like the TenantDb methods already do. `read.findOne` and `read.findMany` steps take a typed table, and the test stack exposes `db` as `DbConnection`.
migration: Type errors show every affected call. A call on a table built from an entity needs no change, its row is derived. On a hand-built table pass the row type, `selectMany<{ readonly jobName: string }>(db, table, where)`, or read a single field as `row["jobName"]`. Type `db` parameters of your own helpers as `DbConnection`, `DbRunner` or `TenantDb` instead of `unknown`. Take row lists as `readonly Row[]`.

title: beforeTransaction keeps outsideTransaction
Live signals wait for the commit
Query handlers declare their result entity
detail: `r.queryHandler({ resultEntity })` applies the entity's field read rules and writeOnly mask to the handler's result (a row, an array of rows or `{ rows }`), as the `entity:verb` naming convention already did. `unfilteredResult: { reason }` marks a query that returns no entity rows. In a feature whose entities have a field with `access.read`, a writeOnly text field or an embedded sub-field with `access.read`, every query handler without a colon in its name must declare one of the two, or the boot fails.
migration: For each query handler the boot names, set `resultEntity` to the entity whose rows it returns. When it returns options, counts or other derived values, set `unfilteredResult: { reason }` with a real reason instead.

title: Breaking changesets declare affects
detail: A `kumiko-changes` block of type breaking without a codemod (or with `manualAfterCodemod`) must carry `affects: <symbol or path>, …` or `affects: all`; parsing fails otherwise. `kumiko changes add` takes `--affects`. `kumiko-upgrade --apply` runs `git grep -F` for these strings in the app after the codemods and records an entry as resolved not-applicable only when nothing matches; any match, a non-git directory or an error leaves it pending.
migration: Add `affects:` to every pending breaking changeset that needs manual work in your repo, or pass `--affects` to `kumiko changes add`.

title: Dashboard panels share one query through resultField
listDefaults replaces bundledLists, adoptsBundledLists removed
detail: The app-wide table block is named `listDefaults` (AppConfig, `ListDefaultsOptions`, `validateListDefaultsOptions`) and applies to every entityList, projectionList and relatedList of every composed feature, app features included. `r.adoptsBundledLists()`, `FeatureDefinition.adoptsBundledLists` and the `adoptsBundledLists` field in feature-manifest.json are removed. The boot rules are renamed from `bundled-lists/*` to `list-defaults/*`.
migration: Rename `bundledLists` to `listDefaults` in kumiko.config.ts and the bin runner options, `BundledListsOptions` to `ListDefaultsOptions`, `validateBundledListsOptions` to `validateListDefaultsOptions`, and delete every `r.adoptsBundledLists()` call. App lists now get the block too; a screen that must differ sets its own `table` keys (`export: undefined`, `pinning: false`, `resizing: false`).

title: EntityRow and EntityExecutorOf exports
Entities carry their name
detail: `createEntity` requires `name`, and `EntityDefinition` has `name`. `r.entity(entity)` or `r.entity({ ...entity, backingTable })`, `r.crud(entity, options?)`, `createEntityExecutor(entity)`, `buildEntityTable(entity, options?)` and `deriveEntityTableMeta(entity, options?)` read it from the entity, so the name given at registration and the one given to the executor can no longer differ.
migration: Run the codemod. It moves the name from `r.entity({ name, ...entity })`, `r.crud("name", entity)`, `createEntityExecutor("name", entity)`, `buildEntityTable("name", entity)` and `deriveEntityTableMeta("name", entity)` into the entity's `createEntity` call and drops the name argument. An entity used under a second name becomes `{ ...entity, name: "other" }` at that site. Entities it cannot resolve are listed as manual; add `name` there by hand.

title: escapeHatch names its grants
detail: `escapeHatch` on write and query handlers, hooks and jobs requires `grants`, a non-empty list of `systemIdentity`, `globalWrites`, `unsafeRaw` and `crossTenantReads`. A declaration without `grants` used to unlock all four; it now fails at boot with "grants is required". `defineProjectionQueryHandler` with `unsafeAllTenants: { reason }` declares `grants: ["systemIdentity"]`. An `escapeHatch` in `r.applyExtension` options takes `{ reason }` only and always means `unsafeRaw`; `grants` there fails at boot.
migration: Run the codemod. It adds the grants it can read from the definition (`unsafeRaw(` for unsafeRaw, `.global(` for globalWrites, `crossTenantReads` for crossTenantReads, `queryAs(`, `writeAs(`, `createSystemUser(`, `unsafeAllTenants` or `runAs` with SystemAdmin for systemIdentity) and lists every other declaration as manual. Add grants to the manual sites by hand and run the integration tests of the touched features: a missing grant only fails when that code path runs. Remove `grants` from `escapeHatch` in `r.applyExtension` options.

title: Typed dispatch through handler contracts
migration: None required. Replace `result as X` and `useQuery<X>(qn, payload)` with a contract exported next to the feature's constants.

title: Registrar verbs take one options object; r.useExtension becomes r.applyExtension
detail: The positional overloads of `r.optionalRequires`, `r.relation`, `r.config`, `r.job`, `r.notification`, `r.readsConfig`, `r.referenceData`, `r.useExtension`, `r.metric`, `r.secret`, `r.secretNamespace`, `r.claimKey` and `r.streamHandler` are removed; each keeps the object form it already had. `r.useExtension` is renamed to `r.applyExtension`, so React lint rules no longer treat it as a hook. The runtime check that rejects positional calls to `r.entity`, `r.writeHandler`, `r.queryHandler`, `r.hook`, `r.requires` and `r.defineWebhookEvent` stays (boot rule `registrar/options-object-required`); only `registrar/argument-missing` is removed with the positional overloads. The boot rule `extension/use-escape-hatch-invalid` is now `extension/apply-escape-hatch-invalid`.
migration: Run the codemod. It rewrites positional calls into the object form, renames `r.useExtension` to `r.applyExtension` and removes the `biome-ignore lint/correctness/useHookAtTopLevel` comment above it. `r.config("key", def)` becomes `r.config({ keys: { key: def } }).key`. Rewrite the sites it lists as manual by hand, and rename `r.useExtension(` in strings and Markdown by hand.

title: defineFailureReasons ties reason slugs to their i18n texts
parentRef and the join features name their hosts
detail: Without an allowlist the parentRef read gate built one SQL branch per registered entity, and the handler executors of tags, folders and notes-history ignored `parents` even when it was set. `ParentRefDef.allowedTypes` is now required, and the boot rule `parent-ref/allowed-types-empty` rejects an empty list. `createTagsFeature`, `createFoldersFeature` and `createNotesHistoryFeature` require `parents`, have no default singleton any more, and build their handler executors with it. `setFolderHandler` and `clearFolderHandler` are removed, and the set, clear and delete folder handlers and `createDeleteTagHandler` take the assignment executor. `folderAssignmentEntity`, `tagAssignmentEntity` and `noteEntryEntity` are the table shape without parentRef. The same holds for signature and document-draft: `createSignatureRequestEntity` and `createDocumentDraftEntity` require the hosts or subject types, `requestExecutor` and `documentDraftExecutor` are replaced by `createSignatureRequestExecutor(hosts)` and `createDocumentDraftExecutor(subjectTypes)`, and the request and draft handler factories take that executor. create-kumiko-app no longer offers tags in the picker.
migration: Pass `parents: [<host entities>]` to every createTagsFeature, createFoldersFeature and createNotesHistoryFeature call and `allowedTypes` to every hand-written parentRef; replace setFolderHandler and clearFolderHandler with the feature mount.

title: Projection system columns come from the event
multiSelect supports optionsQuery on actionForm and configEdit fields
actionForm labelEntity
migration: Optional. Set `labelEntity` on forms whose fields mirror an entity, then delete the `fieldLabels` entries that only point at that entity's field keys and the duplicated `__action-form__` translations.

title: Typed payload for event-triggered jobs
insertProjectedEntityRow and patchProjectedEntityRow for entity rows written by domain events
Entity lists can leave out long fields
Returned query failures are thrown
detail: When a query handler returns a failed `WriteResult`, the dispatcher throws it as a `KumikoError` with the failure's code, status, message and details. `/api/query` answers with that status and error body instead of `200` with `{ data: { isSuccess: false, ... } }`. `ctx.dispatch.query`, `queryAs`, `systemQuery` and the query deps of extra routes and `r.httpRoute` reject, and an extra route that does not catch it answers with the error's status. A query handler can keep `return failNotFound(...)`; callers no longer unwrap `isSuccess` from query results.
migration: Remove code that reads `isSuccess`, `data` or `error` from a query result and catch the thrown error where a caller needs to react to it. An app route that unwrapped a query result for HTTP can return the result directly.

title: Query handler refs type ctx.dispatch.query
Rate limit keyed by the verified caller on signature routes
Cross-tenant aggregate reads
Entity indexes on base time columns
systemDb.scopedTo returns a tenant-filtered db
history binds streamTenantId to the db
Backfill and scrub reach declared verb events
Unmapped colon queries need resultEntity
detail: The boot check that query handlers of a feature with read-restricted or writeOnly fields name their resultEntity skipped every handler with a colon in its name. It now skips only handlers mapped to an entity. A query like "report:overview" with no "report" entity fails the boot until it sets resultEntity or unfilteredResult.
migration: Add resultEntity (the entity whose rows the query returns) or unfilteredResult: { reason } to the reported handler, or rename it to an entity:verb that exists.

title: Row action visibility reads derived fields
onDelete cascades run automatically in the delete lifecycle
detail: Every delete now applies the onDelete strategy of the entity's hasMany and manyToMany relations, after the entity's own preDelete hooks. Cascaded children run their entity preDelete hooks, their postDelete hooks (inTransaction and afterCommit) and recurse into grandchildren. DeleteContext.cascadedFrom names the parent. createCascadeDeleteHook, SystemHookNames and SystemHookPriorities are removed.
migration: Remove createCascadeDeleteHook from systemHooks or lifecycleSystemHooks wiring. Relations that declared onDelete without wiring the hook now cascade or restrict for real; check those declarations. Hand-written cascades in delete handlers can move to onDelete plus entity preDelete hooks.

title: List search through child rows
fromParent ownership rule
Updates reindex only when a search field changes
A record key that an owner forget erases holds only that owner's data
detail: Forgetting a user erases the record key of every row whose owner field holds that user, because the created event keeps the values written while the row had no owner. A `recordOwned` field (`personal: { of: "id" }`) or a `whenAbsent: "self"` field of a second owner field on the same entity sits under that key too, so the erase destroyed the record's own data or another person's, also on rows kept by a `blockDelete` retention. Boot now fails with `pii/record-key-one-owner` when an entity combines `personal: { of: "<ownerField>", whenAbsent: "self" }` with a `recordOwned` field, or uses `whenAbsent: "self"` with more than one owner field.
migration: Give the owner-keyed fields `whenAbsent: "tenant"`, use one owner field for all `whenAbsent: "self"` fields, or keep the record's own data on a separate entity. No bundled feature is affected.

title: Cascade lock check decided by the root delete at every depth
Child-row search requires the child's detail access
Fuzzy-searchable longText fields cannot restrict access.read
detail: The search index is not filtered per role, so a fuzzy-searchable longText with a restricted access.read let roles that cannot read it guess its value from search matches. The boot rule entity/searchable-restricted-read now covers longText like text.
migration: Drop find "fuzzy" or the access.read restriction on the longText field the boot error names.

title: PII backfill keys slim updates by the owner at that event
Validation hooks on one target are chained
Search index keeps up when many tenants write at once
runMigrations checks lockTimeoutMs, system-mode createTenantDb rejects placeholder reasons
migration: Pass a `lockTimeoutMs` of at least 1 or leave it out for the default. Replace a placeholder system-mode reason with the real operator use case.

title: systemScope handlers get ctx.systemDb typed as present
detail: `defineWriteHandler`, `defineQueryHandler` and `definePagedQueryHandler` accept `systemScope: true`. The handler then receives `SystemScopeHandlerContext`, whose `systemDb` is not optional, so the hand-written "ctx.systemDb not wired" checks go away. Boot rejects the marker in a feature without `r.systemScope()` (rule handler/system-scope-without-feature-system-scope), and a dispatch without `ctx.systemDb` (no db wired) throws an InternalError naming the handler. Without the marker nothing changes: `ctx.systemDb` stays optional. `WriteHandlerInput` is now a union over the marker, `defineQueryHandler`/`definePagedQueryHandler` take the new `QueryHandlerInput`, and `WriteHandlerDefinition`/`QueryHandlerDefinition` carry `systemScope?: true`. New helpers: `hasSystemDb` (db) and the type `SystemScopeHandlerContext` (engine). Jobs and hooks keep `requireSystemDb`.
migration: Nothing has to change. To drop a not-wired check, add `systemScope: true` to the handler definition in an `r.systemScope()` feature and replace `requireSystemDb(ctx, "…")` or the `if (!ctx.systemDb) throw …` block with `ctx.systemDb`. An inline `r.writeHandler({ … })` needs `defineWriteHandler(…)` around it for the typed context. A helper taking `HandlerContext` can take `SystemScopeHandlerContext` instead once all its callers declare the marker. A value already typed as `QueryHandlerDefinition` or `WriteHandlerDefinition` can no longer be passed back into `defineQueryHandler`/`defineWriteHandler`; register it directly with `r.queryHandler`/`r.writeHandler`. `systemScope` must be the literal `true`, not a boolean variable.

title: Signature routes can take a raw binary body
A multi-step actionForm hands values to its next step with redirect handOff
File uploads can stay out of the offsite backup
A form screen can name the fields a plain link may fill
_refs carry money and located timestamps in the detail shape
detail: A referenced row in `_refs.<field>` used to hold a money field as the raw minor-unit amount (a `bigint` in process) next to a separate `<field>Currency`, and a located timestamp as `<field>Utc` plus `<field>Tz`. A handler result carrying such a `_refs` row failed in `JSON.stringify`. The row now has the shape the referenced entity's detail query returns: `{ amount, currency }` for money, `{ at, tz, utc }` for a located timestamp, without the companion columns. A money or located timestamp field the caller may not read is absent as a whole; before, its `<field>Currency`, `<field>Utc` or `<field>Tz` column still came through.
migration: Code that reads `_refs.<ref>.<money>` as a number or `_refs.<ref>.<money>Currency` reads `_refs.<ref>.<money>.amount` and `.currency`; code that reads `_refs.<ref>.<ts>Utc` or `<ts>Tz` reads `_refs.<ref>.<ts>.utc` and `.tz`.

title: maxPerTenant defer holds the limit for jobs activated together
Orphan job schedulers are removed while the runner keeps running
stringifyJson on the utils subpath
Migrations fail fast on a blocked table lock
A missing migrations directory fails the prod boot
detail: `detectKumikoDrift` / `assertKumikoSchemaCurrent` treated a missing migrations directory as "no drift", so an image that lost `kumiko/migrations` booted against an unmigrated database. It is now drift: the report has `migrationsDirMissing: true`, `ok: false`, and `runProdApp` / the worker boot abort with a `SchemaDriftError`.
migration: Ship `kumiko/migrations/` in the image or point `migrations.dir` at it. Apps that manage their schema without Kumiko migrations pass `migrations: false`.

title: Projected row helpers accept null to clear an optional field
kumiko-upgrade accepts canary versions from the next dist-tag
custom login methods via session-exchange handlers
A redirect with idFrom opens a custom screen on its record
ROLES.TenantOwner is removed
detail: `ROLES` no longer has a `TenantOwner` entry and `"TenantOwner"` is no longer a reserved platform role name, so an app may declare an `assignableRole` with that name. No bundled feature grants or checks the role any more.
migration: Replace `ROLES.TenantOwner` and the string "TenantOwner" with `Admin` (or `TenantAdmin` where the handler also allows it). Remove `TenantOwner` from role lists and translations.

title: Step and banner actions prefill their target form
PII event backfill stops growing self-owned personal fields
Navigate targets resolve through one shared boot-validator helper
Modal size, labelled action menu and menu item descriptions
Bulk action opens an actionForm with all selected ids
actionForm preview from a query over the form values
Boot validator checks dateOnlyAfterDays on list columns
Boot warns on tenant or user rate limits without a RateLimitResolver
URL prefill and the hidden-required boot rule follow navigate targets given as a QN
ctx.events.loadByTypes reads several aggregates by event type in one query
actionForm redirect with searchParams to custom screens
Board options for dashboards, projectionDetail and forms
Cross-tenant file reads declared per entity
jsonb emptyValue "array" on projection tables
ConfigMask.readOnly shows a key without an input in the settings hub
Boot validation checks the relativeTime timeZone
Form helpers, list pills, phone cells, pinned footer actions and photo grid
CRUD schemas carry the reference target of their fields
Whitespace-only translations and blank plural forms fail the boot check
detail: The locale completeness check at boot treated a value of one space as present, so a button with that label rendered blank, and it treated every plural object as present. Whitespace-only strings and plurals with an empty or whitespace-only form now count as missing, and the i18n parity test applies the same rule to locale bundles.
migration: Fill in each key the boot error lists. For a plural, fill in the blank form or remove it so the lookup falls back to `other`.

title: Irreversible operations without a write-handler entry need a declared exception
detail: A job (`r.job`) or multi-stream projection that runs an irreversible operation without a write-handler entry now throws AccessDeniedError (`irreversible_operation_without_entry_handler`) instead of passing silently. Declare `irreversibleWithoutEntryHandler` with one of `rebuildable-derived-data`, `high-risk-or-cron-pipeline` or `per-dispatch-record-key`. The declaration covers only the job's or consumer's own code; afterCommit hooks, nested dispatches and agent tool calls inside it are still gated. Any other request scope without a write-handler entry is refused too: an afterCommit or afterRollback hook of an HTTP write, an HTTP route, a WebSocket handler. A refused job goes red and a refused consumer goes to the dead letter, while a refused hook is only logged, so its delete does not happen and only the log shows it.
migration: Add `irreversibleWithoutEntryHandler: "<case>"` to each job or multi-stream projection that calls executor.forget, a hard delete, kms.eraseKey or writes a readAsInstruction field. Pick the case that names why no entry handler exists; if none fits, route the operation through a write handler with `agent: { risk: "high" }`. Hooks and routes that call one of these primitives directly must dispatch such a handler or a job instead.

title: Global host gate skips readable hosts and where-rules and caps unpinned lists
Named filter refs carry `access` instead of `roles`
detail: `NamedListFilterRef.roles` is replaced by `access` (an `AccessRule`), set by the framework from the entity filter's rule; an authored `access` is dropped like `roles` was. The client offers a chip with `isUiAccessGranted(ref.access, userRoles)`, so `anySignedIn` and `openToAll` follow the same rules as role-gated screens: `anySignedIn` opens a rule only next to the `anonymous` role, and `openToAll` needs a non-empty reason. Before, every rule form other than a plain role list was offered to everyone. `isNamedFilterOffered` is removed from the renderer.
migration: Remove `roles` from `NamedListFilterRef` literals in screens (it was framework-owned and dropped anyway); the restriction is declared once as `access` on the entity's `namedFilters` entry. Code reading `ref.roles` from a built app schema reads `ref.access` instead.

title: Handlers can no longer call the unbound delivery attempt log factory
One shared derivation of the list query keys the summary-row check expects
Biome preset closes temporal-polyfill completely and tightens plugin gaps
x-kumiko-now is stamped after the handler ran
kumiko CLI commands keep the whole output of the processes they start
Agent tool calls can read global entities
Biome preset biome-rules with GritQL plugins
detail: `@cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/biome-rules` bundles the linter rules and the GritQL plugins that replace the deleted guards, plus the new builtins noNestedComponentDefinitions, noMisusedPromises, useExhaustiveSwitchCases and noTsIgnore. `biome-app` now extends it. Suppress a plugin finding with `biome-ignore lint/plugin: <reason>`. `test-title` and the raw interactive element rule (`a`, `details`, `summary` in `raw-ui-in-app`) only warn, in the framework too, because the replaced guards only warned in repos without a baseline; every other plugin rule is an error. The screen container rule (`mx-auto` + `max-w-*`) is its own plugin `no-screen-container-classes` and does not apply under `public/`. `biome lint` takes about 3.2x as long with the plugins (every regex sits behind a cheap prefilter). The server-side plugins also scan `bin/` and `scripts/`. noImportCycles stays off (253 findings in the framework repo). noRestrictedImports flags type imports of temporal-polyfill too (the old guard allowed them); use `@cosmicdrift/kumiko-types/temporal`. The scaffold main.ts starts with `biome-ignore-all lint/style/noProcessEnv`, since it wires KMS from the environment before runProdApp parses the env contract.
migration: Apps on `biome-app` get the preset automatically; fix new findings or suppress them with a reason. Repos with their own biome.json add `"extends": ["@cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/biome-rules"]`.

title: systemScope queries under queryAsMember get a read-only systemDb
parent-ref gate resolves global hosts in the system scope
reference-data RLS, search hold, scrub coverage, export paging, webhook strictness
consistent schema command names in validate output
JobContext drops the unused _tenantId, ANONYMOUS_ROLE has one definition
Review fixes in document-ingest, documents, feature-toggles, auth-mfa and auth-email-password
detail: appendMissingDocumentExtractEvent returns already-terminal when a concurrent catch-up run wins the append and treats any non-null meta.error as a failure. The documents feature builds hook targets, live entities and the link-list and delete-handler names from its entity constants. createRedisToggleSyncSignal takes the channel prefix and subscribe pattern as one RedisNamespace-shaped argument so they cannot diverge. A test ties TENANT_KEEP_ACCOUNT_ROLES to the account-close roles. Static invite accept returns an unexpected-response failure unless the server answered with an MFA gate. The MFA verify screen reuses MfaCodeOrRecoveryField, trims pasted recovery codes and the preauth setup screen focuses the code field once the recovery codes are acknowledged. Both forgot-password and signup screens share resolveReturnTo. Price env validation uses startsWith instead of an unescaped regex. AppendMissingExtractEventDeps drops the redundant tenantId and relies on tenantDb.tenantId. The framework exports MAX_RETURN_PATH_LENGTH from utils as the single source for the returnTo limit, used by the auth routes and re-exported by the auth-email-password return-path module. Deleting a since-undeclared secret key under a mounted feature prefix works for SystemAdmin and stays unknown-key for tenant admins.

The `tx` handed to the transaction() callback is typed as DbTx (the postgres-js transaction handle it always was at runtime) instead of the Bun.SQL instance type; a helper that takes `db: DbConnection` and receives that tx needs `DbRunner` or `DbTx`.

The positional form createDbConnection(url, options) and the @cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/bun-db subpath keep working as deprecated aliases and are removed in the first release after 2026-10-29.

old -> new:
  createConnection(url, options) (async) -> createDbConnection({ url, ...options }) (sync)
  createPgConnection(url, options) -> createDbConnection({ url, ...options })
  createDbConnection(url, options) -> createDbConnection({ url, ...options }) (positional form is deprecated)
  @cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/bun-db -> @cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/db (deprecated alias until the first release after 2026-10-29)

Removed without replacement: createBunDbConnection, bunDbConnectionOptionsFromEnv, the BunDbConnection, BunDbTx, BunDbRunner and BunDbConnectionOptions types, DbPoolHandle (use DbConnectionHandle), the PgListenClient re-export from /bun-db (import it from @cosmicdrift/kumiko-types/db-connection) and the DB_PROVIDER environment variable.

It rewrites bun-db imports to /db, createDbConnection(url, options) and createConnection/createPgConnection calls to the object form, and reports leftovers (removed Bun.SQL exports, DB_PROVIDER) with file and line. Remove DB_PROVIDER from your env files.

title: Bundled feature constants become create*Feature() factories
detail:
Every bundled feature that was mounted as a constant (tagsFeature, ledgerFeature, authFoundationFeature, ...) now has a create<Name>Feature() factory exported from the same subpath, and apps mount `createTagsFeature()` instead of `tagsFeature`. Factories of features without options take no arguments; the ones that already had options keep them. Two calls of a factory give interchangeable instances, so mounting the same feature from two stacks does not trip the "mounted twice as distinct instances" check.

The old constants keep working as deprecated aliases and are removed in the first release after 2026-10-29.

old -> new:
  tagsFeature -> createTagsFeature()
  ledgerFeature -> createLedgerFeature()
  authFoundationFeature -> createAuthFoundationFeature()
  fooBarFeature -> createFooBarFeature() (same rule for every bundled feature constant)
  typeof tagsFeature -> ReturnType<typeof createTagsFeature>
migration: Run `bun kumiko-upgrade --apply`. It renames the imports and replaces every use with the factory call. It reports aliased imports, re-exports, namespace access, dynamic imports and files that compare a feature by identity with file and line; handle those by hand (one factory call per mount, or keep one shared instance).

title: List filters can no longer probe secret, encrypted or personal fields
whenAbsent "self" keys ownerless personal fields on the record instead of the tenant
migration:
Switching an existing field from `whenAbsent: "tenant"` to `"self"` changes only new writes. Events and rows written earlier stay tenant-keyed (still readable) until the PII event backfill re-keys them. The backfill fingerprint is bumped (`owner-rekey-v2`), so the boot-time backfill runs one more full pass: tenant-keyed values of rows without an owner move under their record key, tenant-keyed values of rows with an owner still move under that owner. The pass rewrites event payloads in place through the existing backfill path and queues the affected projections for rebuild. Apps that run the backfill manually call `backfillEventPiiEncryption` with `resolveOwnerFromProjection: true, rekeyTenantKeyedOwnerFields: true`, then rebuild the projections. Values of a record forgotten earlier become `[[erased]]`. The re-key covers entity lifecycle events only: custom `defineEvent` piiFields that switch from `whenAbsent: "tenant"` to `"self"` keep their old events tenant-keyed.

Old events are never reinterpreted at read time: an old created event of a row that got an owner later keeps its record key until a forget of that record, which erases it, while the later owner-keyed copies stay readable.

detail: Write handlers accept transaction "perCommand". Such a handler runs without a transaction of its own, so every ctx.write and ctx.writeAs it issues runs as its own top-level command with its own transaction, gates and afterCommit hooks. A perCommand handler cannot run as a nested ctx.write, cannot be part of a multi-command batch (422 per_command_handler_in_batch) and cannot combine with beforeTransaction or reserveBeforeTransaction (boot error). ctx.write and ctx.writeAs from stream handlers and top-level query handlers now take the same route, so afterCommit hooks of the called write, which never fired before, fire now. ctx.db writes (entity executor, insertOne, updateMany, deleteMany, db.global() writes) and event appends (appendEvent, unsafeAppendEvent, tryAppendEvent, fetchForWriting, archiveStream, restoreStream, snapshotAggregate) throw in stream handlers, top-level query handlers, perCommand handlers and in beforeTransaction and reserveBeforeTransaction. ctx.dbOutsideTransaction and ctx.outsideTransaction stay available, and ctx.db.unsafeRaw stays open as the audited escape hatch.

title: Secure host-only session cookies use the __Host- prefix
detail: Auth, csrf and tenant cookies are named __Host-kumiko_auth, __Host-kumiko_csrf and __Host-kumiko_tenant when they are written Secure and without a Domain (the tenant cookie is always host-only). With auth.cookieDomain or without Secure the auth and csrf names stay kumiko_auth and kumiko_csrf. New auth option secureCookies forces Secure (default NODE_ENV === "production"). Login deletes the legacy unprefixed host-only cookies, logout and deleteTenantCookie delete the prefixed and the legacy names. The server reads only the resolved names, so a request that carries only the legacy kumiko_auth is anonymous. AUTH_COOKIE_NAME, CSRF_COOKIE_NAME and TENANT_COOKIE_NAME are removed from the framework and dispatcher-live; the base names and sessionCookieName() are exported from @cosmicdrift/kumiko-types/session-cookies and @cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/api, getSessionCookies(c) returns the resolved names of a request. Staging or preview deployments over plain http need no change (Secure is off there); set auth.secureCookies (also accepted by runProdApp) explicitly when TLS terminates before the app and NODE_ENV is not "production". Without allowedOrigins, cookieDomain and unsafeSkipOriginCheck, buildServer mounts the Origin guard for cookie-authenticated state-changing /api requests and admits publicOrigin plus the request's own host (Host header). runProdApp sets publicOrigin from auth.publicOrigin, then auth.mail.baseUrl, then the APP_BASE_URL env (origin only, path dropped); with none of them in production it logs a warning that the Origin guard is off and boots anyway. allowedOrigins keeps its strict meaning, and the WebSocket check and the anonymous downgrade still use only allowedOrigins.

title: Entity PII fields need whenAbsent: "tenant" when the owner field is nullable
detail: personal: { of: "<owner>", whenAbsent: "tenant" } makes rows without an owner editable, deletable and forgettable with an active KMS, without plaintext PII. The subject is resolved in this order: the owner on the previous row, the owner the same event sets, then the tenant key (tenant:<tenantId>). Before, an update, delete or forget of an ownerless row failed with SubjectResolutionError (HTTP 500) once a KMS was configured. backfill-pii follows the same chain and checks the projection row for the owner before it falls back to the tenant key; an updated event whose previous.owner is null but whose changes.owner is set no longer loses the owner. Entity fields have no plaintext fallback, so "tenant" is the only value. bundled jobs: cron and system runs (triggeredById null) now store payload, error and log messages as ciphertext under the system tenant key instead of plaintext.
migration: Boot now aborts for a personal: { of: "<owner>" } field whose owner field is not required and that declares no whenAbsent: [Feature X] Field "f" on entity "e" is personal: { of: "ownerId" }, but "ownerId" is not required — rows without an owner would fail to encrypt (SubjectResolutionError, HTTP 500) on update, delete and forget. Declare { personal: { of: "ownerId", whenAbsent: "tenant" } } to encrypt those rows under the tenant key, or make "ownerId" required: true. Entity fields have no plaintext fallback (fw#3654). Fix: add whenAbsent: "tenant", or make the owner field required: true if every row has one. whenAbsent on personal: { of: "id" } throws at declaration. Existing plaintext job-run rows of cron runs stay readable; new ones are ciphertext.

detail:
Database, event-store consumer, search and Redis review fixes

Reference sorting and search re-check label and read access plus ownership, and a stale search index can no longer surface another tenant's row. A failing dispatcher pass no longer records its error on a consumer whose cursor moved in the meantime and skips a row another pass holds locked. A projection rebuild aborts when the configured blind-index key differs from the one used to build the live table. An array `ne` filter on a jsonb column means "does not contain all of these", matching the entity list filter. `date` columns that still hold a timestamptz log a warning once per column.
`kumiko_event_dispatcher_listen_connected` only drops to 0 on a real connection-loss error and is restored when the pre-check recovers. detail:

migration:
Pass `slots` (for example `kmsSlotsOf(<app>ComposedEnv.schema)`) to `resolvePlatformKeks`, `resolveKmsWiringAsync` and `requireKmsWiringAsync`. In `bin/kumiko.ts`, `runSchemaCli(..., { features })` needs `kmsSlots: kmsSlotsOf(<app>ComposedEnv.schema)` (or `[]` when the app wires no Key Manager slots. With `[]` every `*_CIPHERTEXT` env var is ignored, so an app that ships a ciphertext must pass its slots); without it the CLI exits 1 before applying migrations.
Workspace state at release: show-pony `bin/kumiko.ts` and its copy in the kumiko-platform docs samples still call `runSchemaCli` with `features` only. publicstatus, solon, offlot-app, money-horse, phronexsis and kumiko-studio already pass `kmsSlots` / `slots`.

migration:
New field flag `readAsInstruction: true` on `text`, `longText`, and `jsonb`
fields (`@cosmicdrift/kumiko-types`) marks a field whose value a later run
reads as an instruction — a prompt, rule, or template. Any create/update
whose payload writes such a field must resolve `agent.risk: "high"` on the
directly-dispatched entry handler, or the executor gate denies it with
`access_denied` / `instruction_field_write_requires_high_risk` before any
DB write. This is opt-in per field, but touches every write path once a
field carries the flag — consumer checklist:

1. Mark fields that a later run reads as an instruction (prompts, rules,
   templates) with `readAsInstruction: true`.
2. Update your own handlers that write such a field via
   `executor.create`/`executor.update`, or delegate into one via
   `ctx.write`/`writeAs`, to `agent: { risk: "high" }` — the directly
   called handler must carry it, delegation does not inherit it.
3. Standard entity-convention create/update handlers on an entity with such
   a field now default to "high" automatically; declaring a lower
   `agent.risk` on one is a define-time error, same as the delete floor
   from #3345.
4. An update whose payload doesn't include the flagged field stays allowed
   unchanged — the gate checks payload presence after `preSave`, not
   whether the value actually changed.
5. Not gated: `delete`/`restore` (they don't write the field; the existing
   irreversible-delete floor still applies), and your own domain events
   applied via `ctx.appendEvent` whose projection writes a flagged field —
   route such writes through the executor primitives (`create`/`update`)
   to get the gate.
6. On `create`, a flagged field with a `default` counts as written even if
   the payload omits it — `applyDefaults` runs before the gate. A custom
   mid-risk create handler whose payload leaves the field out is denied
   just the same, and a standard create with `excludeFields` on such a
   field still resolves to "high".

title: createTextField/createLongTextField require an explicit personal-data stance
detail:
Both factories' `overrides` parameter is no longer optional and must
include a `personal` stance:
`{ personal: "self", find: "exact" | "fuzzy" | "none" | "secret" }`
(longText: `find: "none" | "secret"`), `{ personal: "tenant", find: … }`,
`{ personal: { of: "<ownerField>" }, find: … }`, `{ personal: "ref" }`, or
`{ personal: false, reason: "<why this is not personal data>" }`. A
missing/malformed shape throws at the call site (`createTextField(...)` /
`createLongTextField(...)` in the message, with every valid option
listed) instead of silently resolving to an unannotated field — this
also removes the #2918 boot-time deprecation warning, since the shape it
warned about can no longer be constructed.
migration:
Two call forms now throw: `createTextField()` / `createLongTextField()`
with no argument at all, and an options object with no `personal` key,
e.g. `createTextField({ required: true })`. Add a stance to every call:

  createTextField({ personal: "self", find: "exact" })
  createTextField({ personal: "tenant", find: "none" })
  createTextField({ personal: { of: "authorId" }, find: "none" })
  createTextField({ personal: "ref" })
  createTextField({ personal: false, reason: "is_business_data" })

`personal: false` additionally requires a non-empty `reason` string.
`find` is mandatory whenever `personal` names a subject (`"self"` /
`"tenant"` / `{ of }`) — not for `"ref"` or `false`. The #2918 boot-time
deprecation warning for this shape is gone; there's nothing left for it
to warn about.

To find remaining call sites (the #2919 codemod mode below is the
migration tool): `kumiko-guards guards
--guard="Text-Field Personal-Stance Guard"` flags every
statically-decidable call missing a stance. `bun
node_modules/@cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/src/scripts/codemod/pii-personal-migration.ts
<targetDir> --report-stance` classifies unannotated text/longText fields
by name heuristic (direct/user-owned/user-reference/near-miss/
unclassified) to help pick the right stance — it does not add one
automatically, since a wrong guess would be worse than the throw. This
codemod is not wired into `kumiko upgrade --apply`; run it by hand. It
also only transforms fields still carrying the OLD flag-based API
(`pii`/`userOwned`/`tenantOwned`/`subjectRef`/`allowPlaintext`) — a field
with no annotation at all was never in its mapping table and needs a
stance added by hand either way.

title: Irreversible writes now require agent.risk "high" on the directly-dispatched handler
migration:
Any write handler reachable as the directly-dispatched entry point that
performs `executor.forget()` (any entity) or `executor.delete()` on an
entity without `softDelete` must resolve `agent.risk: "high"`, or the
executor gate now denies it with `access_denied` /
`irreversible_operation_requires_high_risk` before any DB read.

Three breaking changes ship together:
1. Add `agent: { risk: "high" }` to your own write handler if it directly
   runs `forget` or a hard `delete` on a non-softDelete entity.
2. Delegating via `ctx.write`/`ctx.writeAs` from a lower-risk handler into
   a high-risk forget/hard-delete handler no longer inherits the inner
   handler's risk — the outermost/entry handler's declared risk governs,
   so the delegating handler itself must be "high".
3. Declaring `agent.risk` below "high" on a standard entity-convention
   delete handler for a non-softDelete entity is now a define-time/boot
   error instead of a silently-accepted setting.

Standard entity-convention delete handlers on a non-softDelete entity now
default to "high" automatically (no more implicit "always allow").

`dispatchToolCall` treats the invoked tool itself as the entry handler,
not the surrounding turn/approve write handler that dispatched it — a
mid-risk "approve" handler can safely invoke a high-risk tool directly,
but a mid-risk tool that itself delegates to a high-risk handler via
`ctx.write`/`writeAs` is still denied per rule 2.

`runAsDirectCallEntry` (framework `/api`) is the one sanctioned entry
boundary: it clears the entry handler so the next dispatch counts as the
directly called one. `dispatchToolCall` uses it because the human
confirmation happens in approve; do not use it to lift a handler past
the floor.

Remaining gap: `afterCommit` hooks, jobs, and event consumers are not
gated by this floor — they have no directly-dispatched entry handler to
attribute risk to.

`mailT` and the renderer's `translateWithFallbacks` resolve plural values

Existing string-only translations keep working unchanged. Code that reads
values back out of a bundle (`TranslationBundle`, `TranslationsByLocale`,
`TranslationEntry`) and annotates them as `string` no longer typechecks:
annotate as `TranslationValue` (from `@cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/ui-types`)
or flatten with `translationValueOtherText(value)`.

title: Centralized client-IP resolver replaces the old first-XFF-entry heuristic
detail:
New `trustedProxyHops` option on `ServerOptions` (default 0 — trusts no
proxy header, only the socket address counts). Precedence:
`options.trustedProxyHops ?? options.auth?.trustedProxyHops ?? 0`.
`requestContext.ip` is now always set for an HTTP request (falls back to
"unknown" instead of being left undefined), so `rateLimit: { per: "ip" }`
handlers reached via `r.httpRoute`/`extraRoutes` systemQuery are never
silently unthrottled. `rate-limit/middleware.ts`'s `globalIpRateLimit`/
`authEndpointRateLimit` and `auth-routes.ts`'s `createAuthRoutes` gained a
`trustedProxyHops`/`clientIpResolver` option and now share the server's
one resolver instance instead of each building their own.
migration:
Apps deployed behind a reverse-proxy/ingress that appends to
X-Forwarded-For must set `trustedProxyHops` (buildServer/runProdApp/
runDevApp top-level option) to the number of trusted hops — usually `1`
for a single ingress. Without it, every client collapses into one shared
rate-limit bucket (safe default, but likely too strict for real traffic).
Apps not behind a proxy need no change; `trustedProxyHops` defaults to 0.

Integration tests that call an `ip`/`ip+handler`-rate-limited handler
repeatedly through `stack.http.raw`/`stack.app.request` (no real socket)
now share one "unknown" bucket instead of skipping the bucket entirely —
a previously-passing test suite can start seeing 429s. Fix by flushing
the rate-limit namespace between test cases (`stack.redis.flushNamespace()`
in `beforeEach`), or by setting `setupTestStack({ trustedProxyHops: 1 })`
and sending a distinct `X-Forwarded-For` per test case. Also check any
test that nulls `context.redis` via `extraContext` to exercise a
handler's own redis-down guard: `setupTestStack` now keeps the L3
rate-limit resolver alive from its own always-real Redis in that case
(an explicit `context.rateLimit` still wins), so a handler-declared
`rateLimit` is enforced instead of throwing `InternalError` for a missing
resolver.

"files: a valid upload (png/jpeg/gif/webp/pdf/doc/docx) under the wrong extension is normalized to its real type instead of rejected, when that type is in the field's accept list or the upload has no accept restriction at all"
detail:
A real PNG or WebP saved with a .jpg extension (a common case for renamed
screenshots or messenger downloads) was rejected with content_mismatch
even when the field's accept explicitly allows png/webp, or when the upload
is unattached and has no accept restriction at all. validateFileContent now
also accepts the field's accept list; when the sniffed byte signature
doesn't match the declared extension but the sniffed type's own extension is
in accept, the upload proceeds under the sniffed mimeType with a storage key
built from the corrected extension, and the response reports the corrected
mimeType. When there is no accept restriction at all, any recognized
signature (png, jpeg, gif, webp, pdf, doc, docx) normalizes the same way.
The original filename is kept as the display name. A sniffed type whose
extension is not in a non-empty accept is still rejected with
content_mismatch.
migration: validateFileContent's signature changes from (fileName: string, content: Uint8Array): string | null to (fileName: string, content: Uint8Array, accept?: readonly string[]): FileContentValidationResult ({kind:"ok"} | {kind:"normalized", extension, mimeType} | {kind:"rejected", error}). A direct caller that checked "if (result)" for an error must switch to checking result.kind === "rejected" and reading result.error — every branch of the new return type is a truthy object, so an unmigrated truthy check would now reject every upload. No caller besides the built-in POST /api/files route calls this function directly today (checked across kumiko-framework, kumiko-enterprise, kumiko-platform, kumiko-studio and every app consumer). buildStorageKey gains an optional trailing extensionOverride parameter; existing calls without it are unaffected.

title: Declared event PII fails closed without a subject KMS (fw#2776)
detail:
`defineEvent` has required an explicit PII stance since fw#2558, but a declared stance still did not guarantee ciphertext in `kumiko_events`. Two paths leaked silently and now fail closed.
Boot: `assertPiiBootInvariants` only looked at entity annotations, so an app whose PII lives exclusively in catalogued events booted without a `kms` adapter and wrote plaintext. It now collects events with a non-`"none"` stance alongside the PII entities — prod aborts, dev warns, `allowPlaintextPii: "<reason>"` acknowledges, same as for entities.
Append: `{ personal: { of: "<ownerField>" } }` skipped encryption whenever the owner field carried no id, so the same event type was ciphertext for user-triggered writes and plaintext for system-triggered ones with no signal. The stance now carries `whenAbsent`: `"tenant"` encrypts under the envelope tenant key, `"plaintext"` is an explicit acknowledgement that the value cannot be crypto-shredded. Registration rejects a nullable owner field without one, and an owner that is empty at append time with no declared fallback aborts the write instead of storing the value in the clear.
`delivery:event:attempt` declares `whenAbsent: "tenant"` — a send whose `recipientId` is null now stores the recipient address under the tenant key instead of in plaintext.
migration:
Three things can newly fail. (1) Boot aborts with `BOOT ABORTED — ... events
[...]` when a mounted feature declares a non-`"none"` `piiFields` stance and
`runProdApp`/`runWorkerApp` gets no `kms`. Pass
`kms: createPgKmsAdapter({ databaseUrl, platformKek })`, or acknowledge the
plaintext with `allowPlaintextPii: "<reason>"` until the KMS is provisioned;
`runDevApp` only warns. (2) Registration aborts when a
`{ personal: { of: "<ownerField>" } }` stance names an owner field the payload
schema allows to be null or undefined. Add `whenAbsent: "tenant"` to encrypt
those writes under the envelope tenant key, or `whenAbsent: "plaintext"` to
declare that the value ships unencrypted and is not crypto-shreddable. The
deprecated `{ subjectField: "<ownerField>" }` form cannot express `whenAbsent`
— move it to the canonical `{ personal: { of: ... } }` form. (3) `append()`
throws `SubjectResolutionError` when the owner field is empty at write time
and the event declared no `whenAbsent`. Registration catches this for
ZodObject payload schemas; a non-object schema surfaces it here. An owner
value that is not a non-empty string — a numeric id, an empty string — counts
as absent, so it takes the same path and needs the same declaration.
Separately, `delivery:event:attempt` rows written with a null `recipientId`
used to hold a plaintext recipient address in `kumiko_events` and in
`store_delivery_attempts`. New rows are tenant-subject ciphertext.
`delivery:query:log` decrypts either form, so the admin log view is unchanged;
tooling that reads `store_delivery_attempts.recipient_address` directly must
go through `decryptStoredPii`. Existing plaintext rows stay readable and are
re-encrypted by `backfillEventPiiEncryption`.

TenantDataHookCtx/UserDataHookCtx.db is a tenant-filtered TenantDb; unfiltered hook access needs r.useExtension({ escapeHatch }) (fw#2914 Zugang 3).
detail:
EXT_TENANT_DATA `destroy` hooks (`TenantDataHookCtx.db`) and EXT_USER_DATA `export`/`delete` hooks (`UserDataHookCtx.db`) no longer receive the unfiltered `DbRunner` that was bound to the extension's owning handler. Both are now a `TenantDb` in "tenant" mode, built via the public `createTenantDb(...)`, bound to the hook's `tenantId`: reads/writes go through `ctx.db.selectMany/fetchOne/insertOne/updateMany/deleteMany`, already scoped to that tenant plus `SYSTEM_TENANT_ID` reference rows. `r.useExtension(EXT_USER_DATA | EXT_TENANT_DATA, entityName, { ... })` gains an `escapeHatch?: { reason: string }` option, validated non-empty at registration time (throws at boot for an empty/whitespace reason). Declaring it grants `ctx.db.unsafeRaw(reason)` inside that entity's hooks — same reason string — which returns the real, unfiltered `DbRunner`; without it, `ctx.db.unsafeRaw(reason)` throws `AccessDeniedError`. Every granted use reports an `"unsafe-raw"` escape-hatch audit event (`{ handler: "userData:<entity>"|"tenantData:<entity>", kind, reason, tenantId, actor }`) through the caller's `_escapeHatchAuditSink` when wired, else a `security:escape-hatch-used` warn-log — same #2861 pattern PR #2934 already applied to the job runner, and the same one fw#2914's earlier JobContext.db and read-step changes already applied elsewhere in the framework. `run-forget-cleanup.ts`/`run-user-export.ts` (user-data-rights) thread `escapeHatchAuditSink`/`actor` from their owning `r.job`'s `ctx._escapeHatchAuditSink`/`ctx.systemUser.id` down to each hook's `TenantDb`, so a declared use is attributed to the real job run, not `"<unattributed>"`.
`asRawClient(ctx.db)` inside a hook now throws immediately: `asRawClient` rejects a `TenantDb`-shaped argument ("received a tenant-scoped TenantDb (ctx.db). Raw SQL helpers do not apply the tenant filter — use a ctx.db.<method>, or ctx.db.unsafeRaw(reason) with escapeHatch: { reason } ..."). The framework's `DbRunner`-typed free functions (`selectMany(db, table, where)`, `fetchOne`, `insertOne`, `updateMany`, `deleteMany`, `createTenantDb(db, tenantId, mode)`, etc. from `@cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/bun-db`/`/db`) now reject `ctx.db` as their first argument at compile time too — `TenantDb` does not structurally satisfy `DbRunner` (no `.unsafe`/`.begin`).
A table built via `createEntity`+`buildEntityTable`+`r.entity(...)` carries the pre-existing `EXECUTOR_ONLY` brand, so `ctx.db.insertOne/updateMany/deleteMany(table, ...)` against it is a compile error by design ("a managed projection is only writable through the executor"); a hook that needs to write such a table directly (bulk hard-delete, jsonb key removal, an UPDATE expression `updateMany`'s literal-value `set` can't express) needs the `escapeHatch` + `ctx.db.unsafeRaw(reason)` route, filtering by tenant/owner in the SQL text itself — the escape hatch removes automatic tenant-filtering, not the hook author's responsibility to filter. A table built via `defineUnmanagedTable` carries no such brand and stays writable through `ctx.db`'s typed methods directly.
This PR's own `custom-fields` user-data-rights wiring (`wire-user-data-rights.ts`) uses the escape hatch for exactly this reason: `selectCustomFieldsHostRows` runs against a dynamic host table name unknown at compile time, so it can't use `ctx.db`'s typed methods. CI's `AST-Guards (shared runner)` step (`@cosmicdriftgamestudio/kumiko-guards@^0.36.0`, pinned) does not yet recognize this call shape — `isEscapeHatchDeclaredFunction` in `guard-escape-hatch-declared.ts` only matches a property/method literally named `handler`, or a direct call to `hook`/`writeHandler`/`queryHandler`/`streamHandler`; `r.useExtension(EXT_USER_DATA, entityName, { export: exportHook, escapeHatch })` matches neither, because `useExtension` isn't in `ESCAPE_HATCH_CALL_METHODS` and the hook property here is `export`/`delete`, never `handler`. This also isn't fixable by baselining from kumiko-framework: `security-baselines/<repo>.json` ships inside the pinned `@cosmicdriftgamestudio/kumiko-guards` npm package itself, and `run-guards.ts`'s own comment states it is rewritten only by "the infra baseline-maintenance run over all repos on main" — never by a consuming repo's local run, and never persisted through a consuming repo's `bun install`. The fix belongs in the guard's owning repo (presumably `infra`, per this workspace's root `CLAUDE.md`): add `useExtension` to `ESCAPE_HATCH_CALL_METHODS`, or otherwise recognize the framework's actual hook-property names (`export`/`delete`/`destroy`), then release a new `@cosmicdriftgamestudio/kumiko-guards` version and bump the range in kumiko-framework's `package.json`. Until that lands, this PR's `AST-Guards (shared runner)` CI check stays red on this one finding; every other check is green.
migration:
A hook that only reads/writes its own tenant through `ctx.db` method calls (`ctx.db.selectMany/fetchOne/insertOne/updateMany/deleteMany`) needs no change — it now gets the same tenant filter every other `TenantDb` consumer already had. A hook that treated `ctx.db` as a raw connection (`asRawClient(ctx.db)`, `ctx.db` passed as the first argument to a free-function `selectMany`/`fetchOne`/`insertOne`/`updateMany`/`deleteMany`/`createTenantDb`, a cast to `DbRunner`/`DbConnection`, or `"raw" in db ? db.raw : db`) must add `escapeHatch: { reason: "<why>" }` to its `r.useExtension(EXT_USER_DATA | EXT_TENANT_DATA, entityName, { ... })` registration and fetch the runner explicitly with `ctx.db.unsafeRaw("<why>")` (same reason string) at the point of use. Prefer converting to `ctx.db`'s typed methods first — reach for `unsafeRaw` only when the target table is `EXECUTOR_ONLY`-branded (a managed `r.entity(...)` table; typed writes reject it by design — see the `EXECUTOR_ONLY`/`WritableTable` note in Detail) or the SQL needs an expression the typed API can't produce (e.g. a jsonb `-` key-removal `UPDATE`). No codemod — cross-hook raw-SQL usage is expected to be rare enough, and tenant-filter-relevant enough, to review by hand per hook. Hand-built `TenantDataHookCtx`/`UserDataHookCtx` objects in tests need `db: createTenantDb(conn, tenantId, "tenant", undefined, undefined, undefined, { unsafeRaw: { reason: "<why>" } })` instead of a plain connection.

Audit at release: kumiko-enterprise has seven user-data hook files across five packages that take `ctx.db` as a raw `DbRunner` argument (`createTenantDb(ctx.db, ctx.tenantId, "system")` and free-function `selectMany(ctx.db, table, where)`). Each needs `escapeHatch` on its `r.useExtension(...)` plus `createTenantDb(ctx.db.unsafeRaw("<why>"), ctx.tenantId, "system")`, and the reads become `ctx.db.selectMany(table, where)` (already tenant-scoped, no "system" mode needed). They must be migrated in kumiko-enterprise itself before it bumps its pinned `@cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework`/`@cosmicdrift/kumiko-types` version, or `tsc` fails.

Guard-version gap: a consumer that declares `escapeHatch` on a `r.useExtension(...)` registration needs a `@cosmicdriftgamestudio/kumiko-guards` release newer than `^0.36.0`; the shared AST guard run of older versions does not recognize it. Bump the guards range before or alongside this migration, not after.

detail: `r.step.read.findOne`/`r.step.read.findMany` no longer read through the raw `DbRunner` bound to `ctx.db` (`tenantDbRunner(ctx.db)`, which bypassed every tenant filter). They now call `selectMany(ctx.db, table, where, opts)` — `ctx.db` is a `TenantDb`, so the same `TenantDb.selectMany` tenant filter that `ctx.db` method-form reads already apply now also applies here: own tenant + `SYSTEM_TENANT_ID` reference rows, and a caller-supplied `where.tenantId` outside that scope is narrowed away instead of passed through. Both steps gain an optional `unsafeAllTenants: { reason: string }` argument; when set, the step reads through `ctx.systemDb.unsafeRaw(reason)` (`r.systemScope()` features, already granted by the feature's own systemScope) or `ctx.db.unsafeRaw(reason)` otherwise — the latter throws `AccessDeniedError` unless the write/query handler declares `escapeHatch: { reason }` — and reports an `"unsafe-raw"` escape-hatch audit event, same as any other `ctx.db.unsafeRaw` use. A read step that intentionally reads across tenants must add `unsafeAllTenants: { reason: "<why the tenant filter cannot apply>" }` to the step AND `escapeHatch: { reason }` (same reason) to the owning write/query handler (or run the step inside an `r.systemScope()` feature, where the grant already exists). No codemod — cross-tenant read-step usage is expected to be rare and needs a real reason per call site.

title: ctx.queryAsMember runs the queried handler inside a Postgres READ ONLY transaction — ctx.db and ctx.db.unsafeRaw writes fail (fw#2902).
detail: `executeQuery` (`pipeline/dispatch-query.ts`) runs every query whose SessionUser has `origin: "member-resolution"` through `runInMemberReadOnlyTransaction` (`pipeline/member-read-only-transaction.ts`): the handler context, the handler, its postQuery hooks and the field-read filter execute inside a savepoint whose first statement is `SET TRANSACTION READ ONLY`. The savepoint is always rolled back — a released one would leave the caller's transaction read-only. With a caller transaction (write handler, in-transaction hook) the savepoint nests into it; without one (query handler, job, `dispatcher.createMemberReader`) the framework opens a pool transaction around the savepoint, holding one connection for the handler's runtime — nested queries' feature/trial gates and rate limits still use their own resolvers, so many concurrent member reads need pool headroom. Inside the subtransaction Postgres rejects switching back via `SET TRANSACTION READ WRITE` (SQLSTATE 25001). Nested `ctx.query` calls inherit the read-only handle; `ctx.queryAs` is now denied for a resolved member principal like the other identity switches (`member_resolution_read_only`), so it cannot reach a context with a writable `dbOutsideTransaction`. Every write — `ctx.db.insertOne`/`updateMany`/`deleteMany`, `ctx.db.unsafeRaw(...)` SQL, `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE/SHARE`, `nextval()`, temp tables — fails with SQLSTATE 25006, surfaced as `AccessDeniedError` (`details.reason` `member_resolution_read_only`, the PG error as `cause`). Feature gate, rate limit, access check and payload validation still run before the transaction opens; membership, principal and auth-claims resolution keep running on the root connection outside it. Handler code that deliberately issues transaction control (`COMMIT`, `RELEASE SAVEPOINT`, `SET SESSION CHARACTERISTICS`) through `unsafeRaw` is not covered — `unsafeRaw` already requires an `escapeHatch` declaration. Top-level `dispatcher.query` and HTTP queries of ordinary users are unchanged.
migration: Find query handlers reached via `ctx.queryAsMember(userId, qn, ...)` (including handlers they call with `ctx.query`) and check them for database side effects: `ctx.db` inserts/updates/deletes, write SQL through `ctx.db.unsafeRaw`, row locks, sequences, temp tables, `ctx.queryAs` calls, or catching a failed statement and continuing (a failed statement now aborts the enclosing transaction). Move such side effects into a write handler called by the original caller, or read the data without writing. Code branching on the raw Postgres error from such a write must branch on `details.reason === "member_resolution_read_only"` instead. Audit at release: bundled-features 0 sites, solon 0, offlot-app 0, money-horse 0, kumiko-enterprise 0 (no consumer calls ctx.queryAsMember yet).
